newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil income distribution improves slightly.
newsitem.headline: Brazil income distribution improves slightly.

text.p: Income distribution in Brazil, one of the world's most lopsided, improved marginally last year, according to a survey published on Friday.

The study by the Planning Ministry's Institute of Applied Economic Research (IPEA) showed that the proportion of people below the poverty line, or earning less than 65 reais ($62.5) a month, fell to 25.1 percent from 33.4 percent in 1994.

The wealthiest 20 percent of the population earned 62.4 percent of Brazil's total income, down from 64.7 percent two years ago, the survey showed. Half of the nation received 12.3 percent of the country's income, up from 11.3 percent.

IPEA said the improvement was mainly due to Brazil's victory over inflation, which fell to 10 percent a year in 1996 from an annual rate of 5,000 percent in early 1994 through the "Plano Real" economic stabilization plan.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's government claims the 30-month-old Plano Real, which Cardoso launched when he was finance minister, has lifted 13 million Brazilians above the poverty line.
But the wealth gap continues to be vast. A United Nations report last June placed Brazil last on a list of 55 countries in terms of wealth distribution.
